_comment: Hand-authored. Bank 5 $8805-$89FA: the status screen's world map drawer, the per-frame cursor handler ($8937) and the power/chip printer ($89CB). The generator for 20-traced.json subtracts these.

regions.name: Map: wait for the pending row
regions.description: WORLD MAP ON THE STATUS SCREEN (`$8805`, called from the open): `LDA $A5 / BNE` spins until `$A5` (the one half-sent background row) is zero, so the frame and map go into an idle queue.

regions.name: Map: the frame
regions.description: X walks the table `$87E4` in fours (`$FF` ends): `$15` := count, `$19:$18` := PPU address, `$14` := tile, `JSR $C036` (`$D5F8`) queues a run of `count AND $7F` tiles (down when bit 7 is set): the box around the map (two horizontal edges, two vertical edges, four corners).

regions.name: Map: set up the walk
regions.description: `$1B:$1A` := `$8A6E` (the world map's first record), `$19:$18` := `$2C02` (nametable 1 row 0, column 2: the first of 12 map rows), `$17` := 0 (the OAM offset for the entrance markers), `$14` := 0 (the map row). The map is 24 x 24 records but is drawn 12 x 12 tiles: each tile covers a 2 x 2 block of records.

regions.name: Map: clear the tile-row buffer
regions.description: `$0150-$015B` (12 bytes) := 0: one nametable row of map tiles, each tile the OR of its four quadrant bits.

regions.name: Map: column := 0
regions.description: `$15` := 0, the map column. It is entered twice per tile row, once for each of the two map rows that make it, without clearing the buffer in between.

regions.name: Map: an empty record?
regions.description: Byte 0 of the record at `($1A)` equal to `$80` is an empty cell: skip to the advance at `$88B9`.

regions.name: Map: is the cell revealed?
regions.description: Byte 1 AND 7 is the key that reveals the cell: 0 = always shown; otherwise key k is tested as bit k-1 of `$04B0` through `$C078`; not held skips the cell. RUN: with `$04B0` = 0 only the key-0 cells appeared; with `$FF` all. RUN: the open `$84CB` on the labyrinth savestate with chosen keys and clear flags.

regions.name: Map: put the cell in the buffer
Map: an area entrance?
regions.description: Byte 0 bit 7 and byte 2 bit 7 must both be set (a special screen that is a corridor gate); either clear skips to the advance.

regions.name: Map: should the marker show?
regions.description: The corridor number is byte 2 AND `$7F`. **Corridor 21:** shown when `($04AA OR $FC) AND $04A9` = `$FF`, i.e. corridors 1-10 are all cleared - and it is **not** hidden again once corridor 21 itself is cleared. **Any other corridor:** `JSR $C07B` (`$EFAC`), shown only while its cleared flag is clear (carry set). RUN: with all flags `FF FF FF` exactly one marker (corridor 21's) remained; with none cleared, the 20 corridor markers appeared (keys `FF`). RUN: the open `$84CB` on the labyrinth savestate with chosen keys and clear flags.

regions.name: Map: write the entrance marker sprite
regions.description: A sprite at OAM offset `$17`: x = column x 4 + `$10`, y = row x 4 + `$3B`, tile 1, attribute 3 (sprite palette 3, red and white), then `$17` += 4. RUN: the sprites of ten random key/flag settings equalled an independent model of this rule in every case (0 to 20 markers).

regions.name: Map: next record
regions.description: `$1A:$1B` += (byte 0 AND `$0F`) + 1, the record length (the `SEC` before the `ADC` is the plus one).

regions.name: Map: next column
regions.description: `$15`++; at 24 the row is finished, else back to `$8853`.

regions.name: Map: next row
regions.description: `$14`++; an odd count means one more map row goes into the same tile row (back to `$884F`); an even count falls into the flush.

regions.name: Map: queue one row of 12 tiles
regions.description: Room for 15 bytes in the PPU queue (`$C04B`), entry `[$0C][$19][$18]` + the 12 buffer bytes (a zero becomes the blank `$20`), the address then += `$20` (next tile row). RUN: all 144 tiles (12 x 12) equalled the model's quadrant-bit tiles in the ten cases, zero showing as `$20`. RUN: the open `$84CB` on the labyrinth savestate with chosen keys and clear flags.

regions.name: Map: more rows?
regions.description: `$14` = 24 ends (RTS); else back to `$8845` for the next tile row.

regions.name: Map: add this cell's quadrant to its tile
regions.description: Bit value: row even 1 / row odd 4, doubled when the column is odd (so 1 top left, 2 top right, 4 bottom left, 8 bottom right); X := column / 2; `$0150,X` OR= the bit. The tile number is the OR, and bank 2 block 3 holds the tile for each of the 15 values (see the open).

regions.name: STATUS SCREEN, EVERY FRAME (slot `$8021`, called from `$E506`): any button?
regions.description: `$F5 OR $F6` is the pads' NEW presses (both ports), `$F7 OR $F8` the HELD buttons. A new press goes to `$8951`; nothing held ends at `$89C5`; held without a new press goes on to the repeat counter. The wait for Start/Select to leave is `$E509-$E50D` in the caller, not here.

regions.name: Cursor: auto-repeat
regions.description: `$15` is decremented; not yet zero ends at `$89C5`; zero reloads it with 6. A new press (`$8951`) loads 20 instead. RUN (hold Right from a new press): moves at calls 0, 20, 26, 32, 38, 44: one at once, the next after 20 calls, then every 6.

regions.name: Cursor: first-press delay
regions.description: A := 20, stored in `$15` at `$8953` (6 comes in here from `$894D`).

regions.name: Cursor: direction
regions.description: The held buttons' low four bits (Right 1, Left 2, Down 4, Up 8); none ends at `$89C5`. This is also where an unowned weapon sends control back to keep moving.

regions.name: Cursor: Right
regions.description: `$3C`++; 13 wraps to 0.

regions.name: Cursor: Left
regions.description: `$3C`--; below 0 becomes 12.

regions.name: Cursor: Up
regions.description: `$3C` - 5 if that is not negative, else `$3C` + 10, and if that is 13 or more, `$3C` + 5. The cursor positions are 0 (no weapon) and 1-12 in rows of five. RUN: all 13 positions x 4 directions with every weapon owned equalled this reading and its Down twin (Up: 0->10, 1->11, 2->12, 3->8, 5->0, 12->7).

regions.name: Cursor: Down
regions.description: `$3C` + 5 if under 13; 15 or more: minus 15 more; 13 or 14: minus 10 (carry clear), so Down from 8 is 3 and from 10 is 0.

regions.name: Cursor: store
regions.description: `STA $3C`.

regions.name: Cursor: sound, and the weapon's level
regions.description: Sound `$3E` (`$D852`), then `JSR $C135` (`$FD77`), which puts the weapon's level in `$3D` (the notes on weapons).

regions.name: Cursor: skip a weapon that is not owned
regions.description: `$3C` zero (no weapon) is always allowed; otherwise `$3D` zero (level 0, not owned) goes back to `$8955` and moves again in the held direction. RUN: with weapons 2, 5 and 12 owned, Right from 0 gave 2, 5, 12, 0, 2; Left from 0 gave 12.

regions.name: Cursor: refresh the HUD and the numbers
regions.description: `JSR $86ED` (the SHOT icon), `JSR $C072` (the uses left), `JSR $89CB` (power and chips per use).

regions.name: Every frame: the blinking marker
regions.description: Far call (inline `02 1D 80`) to bank 2 `$801E` (-> `$8998`), reached from every path of the handler. The return address skips the inline bytes and the code runs on into `$89CB`, so the numbers are also reprinted on every frame.

regions.name: Print the weapon's power
regions.description: Room for 4 bytes, entry `[01][$2D][$3D][$3D + $30]`: the level `$3D` as an ASCII digit at PPU `$2D3D` (row 9, column 29), next to WEAPON POWER. RUN: `$3D` = 3 gave '3'.

regions.name: Print the chips per use
regions.description: `$19:$18` := `$2D5B` and A := `$45` (the chips one use costs, `$FDD3` table), `JMP $C051` (`$E1CD`): three blank-suppressed digits at row 10, columns 27-29. RUN: `$45` = 25 gave ' 25'.
